population: Anti-EGFR-refractory KRAS-WT (Sym004, zalutumumab) and KRAS-mutant (imgatuzumab) mCRC
note: The non-approved anti-EGFR antibodies in CRC: Sym004 (futuximab+modotuximab) built on resistance models that it beat in phase 1 but not in a randomized phase 2, imgatuzumab's ADCC xenografts predicted KRAS-mutant activity that never appeared, and zalutumumab's CRC trial was too small to test anything; cetuximab and panitumumab are not members of this tile.
label: Colorectal (anti-EGFR mAbs)

engagement.judgement: Opens the Sym004 track: the model's PD readout is loss of surface EGFR (internalization and degradation) in cells and xenografts. No regulator filing exists for any member (all three programs stopped before NDA/BLA), so model_filed is false throughout.
engagement.model: EGFR-expressing cancer cell lines and A431 xenografts (Sym004)
engagement.note: Sym004 (futuximab+modotuximab) strips EGFR from the cell surface by internalization and degradation, unlike cetuximab; no patient readout yet.
engagement.short: Sym004 degrades EGFR in cells and xenografts
engagement.quote: However, unlike the other antibodies, Sym004 induces rapid and efficient removal of the receptor from the cancer cell surface by triggering EGFR internalization and degradation.

engagement.magnitude_basis: membrane EGFR histoscore fell in 16/22 paired tumour biopsies and 32/33 paired skin biopsies; the xenograft papers give no comparable fraction
engagement.population: KRAS exon 2 wild-type mCRC with acquired resistance to cetuximab/panitumumab
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (AACR page). NCT01117428 results first posted 2017-07-12; the paper is the earlier public comparison, so year is 2015.
engagement.judgement: Readout tier direct: the model's readout is the target protein itself leaving the cell surface, measured in patients as membrane EGFR histoscore in tumour (16/22 fell, P=0.0004) and skin (32/33) at week 4. The paper itself frames this as clinical proof of the preclinical mechanism, so comparison_stated is true.
engagement.model: EGFR-expressing cancer cell lines and A431 xenografts (Sym004)
engagement.note: Paired tumour and skin biopsies in anti-EGFR-refractory mCRC showed durable membrane EGFR downmodulation at week 4, the degradation the cell and xenograft work predicted.
engagement.short: Tumour and skin EGFR fell in patients
engagement.quote: Pharmacodynamic studies confirmed marked Sym004-induced EGFR downmodulation.

engagement.magnitude_basis: EGFR ECD mutant allele fraction in ctDNA fell on Sym004; no numeric model-to-patient ratio
engagement.population: KRAS exon 2 wild-type mCRC with acquired resistance to cetuximab/panitumumab
engagement.judgement: Strengthens, same status: the EGFR-ECD-mutant clones the 2016 cell work said Sym004 still binds were suppressed in patients' ctDNA, a downstream readout; this engagement did not translate into benefit (see efficacy).
engagement.model: EGFR-expressing cancer cell lines and A431 xenografts (Sym004)
engagement.note: Phase 2 ctDNA: EGFR ECD-mutant allele fractions fell on Sym004, as the ECD-mutant cell lines predicted; engagement without clinical benefit.
engagement.short: ctDNA EGFR ECD clones fell on Sym004
engagement.quote: Sym004 effectively targeted EGFR ECD-mutated cancer cells, and a decrease in EGFR ECD ctDNA occurred in Sym004-treated patients.
engagement.reason: Target loss seen in tumour, skin, ctDNA

engagement.judgement: Opens the imgatuzumab track at its first public use (epub 2012-12-03). The model's readout is Fc-mediated ADCC by NK cells, not EGFR signalling blockade, which GA201 inhibits no better than cetuximab. The phase 1 (NCT00721266, 2008-2011) used the model earlier but describes it only as 'enhanced ADCC'.
engagement.model: Orthotopic KRAS-WT and KRAS-mutant xenografts with NK-cell ADCC assays (GA201)
engagement.note: Glycoengineered GA201 raised NK-cell ADCC against KRAS-wild-type and KRAS-mutant lines (A549, LS174-T, HT29); no patient readout yet.
engagement.short: GA201 enhances ADCC against KRAS-mutant cells
engagement.quote: This resulted in significantly enhanced induction of ADCC compared with cetuximab against both KRAS-wild-type and -mutant tumor cells lines.

engagement.magnitude_basis: tumour-infiltrating immune cells 1491 vs 898 cells/mm3 after one cycle; the model reports ADCC lysis, not infiltration
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Delord 2014 (Eur J Cancer, paywalled). NCT00721266 (the parent phase 1 with this expansion) has no posted results, so registry_date is null.
engagement.judgement: Downstream readout: immune-effector infiltration into tumour and the fall in circulating NK cells are consequences of the Fc-mediated mechanism, not the target. Paired by me with Gerdes 2013; Delord's abstract infers the mechanism but does not set the xenograft data beside the biopsies.
engagement.model: Orthotopic KRAS-WT and KRAS-mutant xenografts with NK-cell ADCC assays (GA201)
engagement.note: In 25 KRAS-mutant mCRC patients, paired biopsies showed immune-effector infiltration rising after one cycle while circulating NK cells fell: the ADCC mechanism engaged.
engagement.short: Immune infiltration rose in KRAS-mutant tumours
engagement.quote: the number of tumour-infiltrating immune cells increased notably after one cycle of therapy (median compound immune reactive score of 1491 versus 898 cells/mm(3) at baseline), whereas the number of peripheral natural killer cells decreased
engagement.reason: ADCC mechanism engaged; no benefit followed

engagement.judgement: Zalutumumab (2F8) is a member through one CRC trial (NCT00677924, cetuximab-refractory mCRC, n=9, terminated 'due to changes in portfolio review', results posted 2011-12-23) that reported no PK or PD readout, so the A431 model's signalling-blockade and ADCC readouts were never compared in CRC patients. SCCHN PK (Bastholt 2007) is another indication and the dose cell has no import field.
engagement.model: A431 epidermoid xenografts in athymic mice (zalutumumab/2F8)
engagement.note: 2F8 blocked EGFR signalling at saturating concentrations and killed by ADCC at low occupancy in A431 cells and xenografts; no CRC patient PD readout was ever published.
engagement.short: A431 model; no CRC patient PD readout
engagement.quote: At saturating concentrations, 2F8 completely blocked EGF-R signaling and inhibited the in vitro proliferation of EGF-R-overexpressing A431 cells.
engagement.reason: No CRC patient readout to compare

engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC3950873): received 2013-10-24, online 2014-02-04, print 2014-03-04. NK degranulation (CD107a) against A431 targets; ADCC preserved pre-, on- and post-chemotherapy.
engagement.model: Ex-vivo NK cells from mCRC patients before, during and after chemotherapy, GA201-induced ADCC against A431 (imgatuzumab)
engagement.note: Patient NK cells, impaired for natural cytotoxicity, still degranulated against GA201-coated A431 cells at every chemotherapy stage; readout is ex-vivo NK ADCC.
engagement.short: Patient NK cells kill on GA201 ex vivo
engagement.quote: However, GA201 was able to induce robust NK cell-dependent cytotoxicity in CRC patient NK cells, effectively overcoming their impairment.
engagement.judgement: A patient ex-vivo system distinct from the Roche orthotopic xenografts: the effector cells are the patients' own NK cells sampled around chemotherapy, and the prediction is that ADCC survives chemotherapy. Opens at the online date.
engagement.population: mCRC patients pre-, on- and post-chemotherapy (peripheral NK cells ex vivo)

engagement.magnitude_basis: tumour-infiltrating immune cells 1491 vs 898 cells/mm3 and peripheral NK decrease; the ex-vivo assay reports degranulation, no shared quantity
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Delord 2014 (Eur J Cancer, online 2013-11-18, print 2014-02); the pairing was first possible when the ex-vivo paper went online (2014-02-04). Readouts differ: ex-vivo degranulation against A431 versus in-vivo NK decline and tumour infiltration. NCT00721266 has no posted results. Temam 2017 (HNSCC window study, NCT01046266) later showed the NK decline with imgatuzumab but not cetuximab; another indication, so not entered here.
engagement.model: Ex-vivo NK cells from mCRC patients before, during and after chemotherapy, GA201-induced ADCC against A431 (imgatuzumab)
engagement.note: In 25 KRAS-mutant mCRC patients, peripheral NK cells fell and tumour immune-effector infiltration rose after one imgatuzumab cycle: the NK engagement the ex-vivo assay showed.
engagement.short: Patient NK cells engaged in vivo
engagement.quote: the number of tumour-infiltrating immune cells increased notably after one cycle of therapy (median compound immune reactive score of 1491 versus 898 cells/mm(3) at baseline), whereas the number of peripheral natural killer cells decreased
engagement.judgement: The ex-vivo prediction was that patients' NK cells respond to GA201; the dosed patients showed NK redistribution and immune infiltration, a downstream sign of the same engagement. Paired by me: Delord was online before the ex-vivo paper and cannot cite it.
engagement.reason: Patient NK cells moved on dosing

engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5620195): received 2016-12-05, online 2017-06-27, print collection 2017-09-15. Western blots at 5 ug/ml in GEO-CR and SW48-CR; the phase 2 (Montagut 2018) measured ctDNA, not tumour MET/AKT/MAPK phosphorylation. EGFR downmodulation in patient biopsies (Dienstmann 2015) belongs to the Sym004 platform track.
engagement.model: CRC lines with acquired cetuximab resistance and MET activation (GEO-CR, SW48-CR, LIM1215-CR, CACO2-CR) and SW48 xenografts treated at progression on cetuximab (Sym004)
engagement.note: Sym004 shut off MET, AKT and MAPK phosphorylation and drove EGFR degradation in cetuximab-resistant CRC cells; this signalling readout was never measured in Sym004-treated patients.
engagement.short: Sym004 silences MET/AKT/MAPK in resistant cells
engagement.quote: SYM004 treatment determined a significant induction of apoptosis and a strong inhibition of MET, AKT and MAPK phosphorilation in these resistant models.
engagement.judgement: A Naples-lab system distinct from Symphogen's A431 and EGFR-ECD-mutant lines: resistance was selected in vitro against cetuximab and runs through MET, and the model's PD readout is downstream MET/AKT/MAPK signalling, which no patient study of Sym004 read. Never compared.
engagement.reason: Signalling readout never measured in patients
engagement.population: CRC lines with in-vitro-acquired cetuximab resistance (MET-activated GEO-CR, SW48-CR; LIM1215-CR, CACO2-CR) and nude-mouse xenografts

dose.judgement: Opens the dose strip: Skartved 2011 gives mouse-xenograft PK (50 mg/kg single dose) and monkey PK at 2-24 mg/kg weekly without stating a human exposure target or an efficacious-exposure multiple, so margin_stated is false and decision 16 is not applied.
dose.model: A431NS xenograft PK and cynomolgus repeat-dose PK (Sym004)
dose.note: Monkeys got 2-24 mg/kg weekly with dose-proportional exposure and no accumulation; no human exposure target was stated.
dose.short: Monkey PK 2-24 mg/kg; no human target
dose.quote: Monkeys received once weekly intravenous infusions of Sym004 in the range 2 to 24 mg/kg for 6 to 8 weeks.

dose.magnitude_basis: model-level target effect (EGFR degradation) reproduced in patient biopsies at 9-12 mg/kg weekly; no exposure ratio stated
dose.population: KRAS exon 2 wild-type mCRC with acquired resistance to cetuximab/panitumumab
dose.confidence_note: Full text read. Escalation stopped at 12 mg/kg on late skin and hypomagnesaemia toxicity; 9 and 12 mg/kg were both carried into expansion with responses at each.
dose.judgement: Scored same because the regimen reached the model's target effect in tumour (EGFR downmodulation) and produced responses, i.e. the dose was reached and was enough for the phase 1 gate. Not margin_stated: the monkey study placed no tolerated dose against an effective exposure, and the human escalation was capped by cumulative skin and magnesium toxicity rather than a formal MTD.
dose.model: A431NS xenograft PK and cynomolgus repeat-dose PK (Sym004)
dose.note: Weekly 9-12 mg/kg reproduced the model's EGFR loss in patient tumours and gave partial responses; escalation stopped at 12 mg/kg on cumulative skin and magnesium toxicity.
dose.short: 9-12 mg/kg hit target effect, with toxicity
dose.quote: A formal MTD was not reached, and the maximum administered dose, declared in a joint decision of the investigators, sponsor, and the independent data-monitoring committee, was set at 12 mg/kg.

dose.judgement: Opens the imgatuzumab dose strip. The xenografts used a flat 25 mg/kg weekly with no human exposure target; the clinical 1,400 mg regimen was chosen on human PK modelling (clearance plateau above 400 mg, Paz-Ares 2011), not on the model.
dose.model: Orthotopic KRAS-WT and KRAS-mutant xenografts with NK-cell ADCC assays (GA201)
dose.note: Xenografts were dosed 25 mg/kg weekly against cetuximab at the same dose; the human dose was set on PK modelling, no model exposure target.
dose.short: Mouse 25 mg/kg weekly; no human target
dose.quote: GA201, cetuximab, panitumumab, and the corresponding vehicle (control) were administered intravenously once weekly for 3 weeks at a dosage of 25 mg/kg.

dose.magnitude_basis: no objective responses in 25 patients at the receptor-saturating 1,400 mg regimen; the model gave no exposure target
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Delord 2014. Paz-Ares 2011 (full abstract) shows clearance plateaued above 400 mg, so 1,400 mg q2w saturates target-mediated clearance.
dose.judgement: Dose scored on its own prediction (rule v4): 1,400 mg saturated EGFR-mediated clearance and engaged ADCC. Derived from efficacy (reached, failed, abandoned): the 1,400 mg regimen saturated EGFR-mediated clearance and engaged the immune mechanism in tumour (engagement cell), so the KRAS-mutant failure is charged to the model, not to dose. GAIN-C (2015) then failed at the same regimen and Roche stopped the program. No independent toxicity block: no MTD was reached in phase 1.
dose.model: Orthotopic KRAS-WT and KRAS-mutant xenografts with NK-cell ADCC assays (GA201)
dose.note: 1,400 mg day 1/8 then q2w saturated clearance and engaged ADCC in KRAS-mutant tumours, yet gave no responses; the regimen was adequate, the prediction was not.
dose.quote: Patients received single-agent imgatuzumab (1400mg on day 1 and 8 followed by q2W) as third line therapy in an open-label, multicentre, non-randomised, expansion study.

dose.population: Unselected (A431 and lower-EGFR xenografts; cynomolgus PK)
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Lammerts van Bueren 2006.
dose.judgement: The model's dose statement is receptor-saturation PK: tumour EGFR saturation needs high plasma levels and monkey clearance is nonlinear at low dose. The only CRC trial (NCT00677924, 8 and 16 mg/kg with irinotecan, n=9) posted AE and response counts but no PK, so the target was never checked in CRC patients; the SCCHN saturation PK (Bastholt 2007) is another indication.
dose.model: A431 epidermoid xenografts in athymic mice (zalutumumab/2F8)
dose.note: Receptor-mediated clearance model: A431 tumours need high plasma 2F8 for EGFR saturation; the 9-patient CRC trial posted no PK, so never compared.
dose.short: Saturation PK model; no CRC PK published
dose.quote: Ex vivo analyses of xenograft tumors of 2F8-treated nude mice revealed that relatively high antibody plasma concentrations were required for maximum EGFR saturation in high-EGFR-expressing human A431 tumors, in contrast to lower-EGFR-expressing human xenograft tumors.
dose.reason: No CRC exposure data to compare

dose.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5620195). Both the de novo xenografts (SW48, LIM1215, CACO2; n=10 per arm, 30 weeks) and the treat-at-progression SW48 model (n=7) used 50 mg/kg twice weekly; no PK and no tolerated-dose statement.
dose.model: CRC lines with acquired cetuximab resistance and MET activation (GEO-CR, SW48-CR, LIM1215-CR, CACO2-CR) and SW48 xenografts treated at progression on cetuximab (Sym004)
dose.note: Xenografts got Sym004 50 mg/kg i.p. twice weekly against cetuximab 1 mg twice weekly for up to 30 weeks; no human exposure target was stated.
dose.short: 50 mg/kg twice weekly, no human target
dose.quote: At progression phase mice were assigned to SYM004 treatment (50 mg/Kg twice a week) by i.p. injection.
dose.judgement: A regimen, not an exposure target: the model states a mouse dose and a comparator dose but nothing that maps to a human exposure, so the cell opens untested.
dose.population: CRC lines with in-vitro-acquired cetuximab resistance (MET-activated GEO-CR, SW48-CR; LIM1215-CR, CACO2-CR) and nude-mouse xenografts

efficacy.judgement: Opens the Sym004 efficacy track. Pedersen 2010 is the class-level prediction (superior to cetuximab in xenografts); the acquired-resistance predictions came later on the same platform: ligand-driven resistance (Dienstmann 2015 preclinical section), cetuximab-resistant NCI-H226 xenografts (Iida 2013, doi:10.1593/neo.131584) and EGFR-ECD-mutant CRC lines (Sanchez-Martin 2016).
efficacy.model: EGFR-expressing cell lines and xenografts incl. cetuximab-resistant and EGFR-ECD-mutant CRC lines (Sym004)
efficacy.note: Sym004 out-performed cetuximab in vitro and in xenografts; no patient result yet.
efficacy.quote: Compared with reference anti-EGFR monoclonal antibodies, Sym004 exhibited more pronounced growth inhibition in vitro and superior efficacy in vivo.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: 13% partial response and 44% tumour shrinkage in 39 expansion patients vs xenograft regression; not commensurable
efficacy.population: KRAS exon 2 wild-type mCRC with acquired resistance to cetuximab/panitumumab
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read. The registry primary outcome of NCT01117428 is adverse events; the expansion cohorts were the sponsor's activity gate in anti-EGFR-refractory mCRC, hence endpoint_role poc_gate.
efficacy.judgement: Scored same on the proof-of-concept gate: the paper states the activity 'validates the preclinical hypothesis that a proportion of tumors remains dependent on EGFR signaling' (comparison_stated). Single-arm, 39 patients, so medium magnitude confidence; the randomized test came in 2018.
efficacy.model: EGFR-expressing cell lines and xenografts incl. cetuximab-resistant and EGFR-ECD-mutant CRC lines (Sym004)
efficacy.note: Phase 1 expansion in anti-EGFR-refractory mCRC: 5/39 partial responses (13%) and 44% tumour shrinkage at 9-12 mg/kg, the activity the resistance models predicted.
efficacy.quote: In dose-expansion cohorts of 9 and 12 mg/kg of Sym004 weekly, patients with metastatic colorectal cancer and acquired EGFR inhibitor resistance were enrolled; 17 of 39 patients (44%) had tumor shrinkage, with 5 patients (13%) achieving partial response.

patient_trials.quote: 17 of 39 patients (44%) had tumor shrinkage, with 5 patients (13%) achieving partial response.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: one patient (G465R) benefited; xenograft showed profound regression
efficacy.population: mCRC with EGFR extracellular-domain mutation after cetuximab
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Clin Cancer Res, paywalled); n=1 patient from the phase 1 (NCT01117428).
efficacy.judgement: Strengthens, same status, patient-level: the ECD-mutant cell lines and xenograft said Sym004 still binds and regresses tumours carrying G465R/S492R, and one such patient responded. Also the prediction the 2018 trial then tested and refuted.
efficacy.model: EGFR-expressing cell lines and xenografts incl. cetuximab-resistant and EGFR-ECD-mutant CRC lines (Sym004)
efficacy.note: EGFR-ECD-mutant CRC cells and xenografts stayed Sym004-sensitive; a G465R patient from the phase 1 benefited, a one-patient proof of principle.
efficacy.quote: As proof-of-principle, a patient with a tumor harboring an EGFR mutation (G465R) following cetuximab therapy benefited from Sym004 therapy.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: OS HR 1.31 (A vs C) and 0.97 (B vs C); model predicted benefit, none in the ITT or in EGFR-ECD-mutant patients
efficacy.population: KRAS exon 2 wild-type mCRC with acquired resistance to cetuximab/panitumumab
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5885274). Registry NCT02083653 results first posted 2018-12-24; the paper is the earlier public comparison. EU-CTR 2013-003829-29.
efficacy.judgement: Contra on the primary endpoint (OS, ITT) and on the patient-level prediction: the paper states that preclinical efficacy in EGFR ECD-mutated cells and the ctDNA fall in those clones 'was not linked to clinical benefit of Sym004 in the present trial'. The exploratory ctDNA-defined RAS/BRAF/EGFR-ECD-negative subgroup (median OS 12.8 vs 7.3 months, arm B vs C) is retrospective and hypothesis-generating by the authors' own words, and was never prospectively tested (NCT03549338 enrolled 2), so it does not lift the status. The 12 mg/kg arm was worse than control (HR 1.31).
efficacy.model: EGFR-expressing cell lines and xenografts incl. cetuximab-resistant and EGFR-ECD-mutant CRC lines (Sym004)
efficacy.note: Randomized phase 2 in anti-EGFR-refractory mCRC: OS not improved (HR 1.31 and 0.97 vs investigator's choice); EGFR-ECD-mutant patients, the model's biomarker, gained nothing.
efficacy.short: Phase 2 OS failed; ECD biomarker failed
efficacy.quote: Sym004 did not improve OS in an unselected population of patients with mCRC and acquired anti-EGFR resistance.

patient_trials.quote: A subgroup of patients was defined by ctDNA (RAS/BRAF/EGFR ECD-mutation negative) associated with improved OS in Sym004-treated patients in arm B compared with arm C (median OS, 12.8 and 7.3 months, respectively).
Discontinued development of Sym004 in combination with FOLFIRI

efficacy.reason: OS and ECD-biomarker predictions both failed

efficacy.magnitude_basis: poor or limited PDX activity in RAS/BRAF-mutant models vs no OS benefit in RAS/BRAF-mutant ctDNA patients
efficacy.population: KRAS exon 2 wild-type mCRC with acquired resistance to cetuximab/panitumumab
efficacy.confidence_note: PDX data are in eFigure 11 of the paper's supplement, read only through the main-text sentence.
efficacy.judgement: Separate track and a retrodiction (decision 10): the RAS/BRAF-mutant PDX panel was run alongside the trial, after the clinic already knew RAS/BRAF-mutant tumours resist anti-EGFR antibodies, and reproduced it; scored retro, never same. No prospective PDX prediction for this class followed.
efficacy.model: Patient-derived CRC xenografts with RAS/BRAF mutations (Sym004)
efficacy.note: PDX panel run with the trial: RAS- and BRAF-V600E-mutant xenografts barely responded to Sym004, matching the ctDNA-defined non-benefit in patients, a retrodiction.
efficacy.quote: In preclinical patient-derived xenograft CRC models with RAS and BRAF V600E mutations, poor or limited Sym004 activity was observed, indicating that clonal mutations in these genes caused resistance to Sym004, as is the case for cetuximab and panitumumab

efficacy.judgement: Opens the imgatuzumab track: orthotopic LS174-T (KRAS G12D) and HT29 liver-metastasis CRC models plus A549 lung; the paper's own clinical prediction is 'a first-in-class treatment of patients with KRAS-mutated tumors'. Full text read via the AACR page.
efficacy.model: Orthotopic KRAS-WT and KRAS-mutant xenografts with NK-cell ADCC assays (GA201)
efficacy.note: Orthotopic KRAS-mutant and wild-type xenografts (LS174-T, HT29, A549) responded to GA201 better than to cetuximab; prediction: KRAS-mutant patients will respond via ADCC.
efficacy.quote: This superior efficacy of GA201 was seen in both KRAS-mutant and KRAS-wild-type mouse xenograft models and was further enhanced when combined with irinotecan chemotherapy.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: 0/25 objective responses (primary endpoint tumour response) vs superior xenograft efficacy in KRAS-mutant models
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Delord 2014; the expansion sits inside NCT00721266, which has no posted results. Paz-Ares 2011 (doi:10.1200/JCO.2011.34.8888) reported one KRAS-mutant CRC response among 75 mixed phase 1 patients before the model was published; it is a mixed-tumour cohort and does not change this call.
efficacy.judgement: Contra, patient-level: the model's stated prediction was efficacy in KRAS-mutant tumours through ADCC; the dedicated KRAS-mutant mCRC cohort met its primary endpoint of tumour response with zero responses and stable disease in 40% at 8 weeks. Paired by me (Delord's abstract does not set the xenografts beside the result).
efficacy.model: Orthotopic KRAS-WT and KRAS-mutant xenografts with NK-cell ADCC assays (GA201)
efficacy.note: Single-agent imgatuzumab in 25 KRAS-mutant mCRC patients: no objective responses, best response stable disease (40% at 8 weeks); the KRAS-mutant xenograft prediction failed.
efficacy.quote: 25 patients were treated and the best overall response was stable disease occurring in 40% of patients at 8weeks, 24% at 16weeks and 8% (two patients) at 32weeks.

patient_trials.quote: Median overall survival was 9.3months (95% confidence interval (CI): 5.1-12.3).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: PFS HR 0.94 (imgatuzumab+FOLFIRI vs FOLFIRI, KRAS-mutant) and 1.13 (vs cetuximab+FOLFIRI, KRAS-WT); model predicted superiority to cetuximab and activity in KRAS-mutant
efficacy.population: Second-line mCRC, KRAS exon 2 wild-type and mutant
efficacy.confidence_note: ASCO GI 2015 meeting abstract (DOI 10.1200/jco.2015.33.3_suppl.669), not a full paper; NCT01326000 (169 randomized) has no posted results and no journal publication was found. Tier 1 by its DOI, but weight it as an abstract.
efficacy.judgement: Strengthens the contra at class level: GAIN-C tested both of the model's predictions, superiority over cetuximab in KRAS-WT (PFS HR 1.13) and benefit over chemotherapy alone in KRAS-mutant (HR 0.94), and the sponsor called the primary endpoint negative in both; Roche then stopped imgatuzumab (the 2014 squamous NSCLC study was withdrawn). Grade 3+ rash 42.5% and hypomagnesaemia 30% on imgatuzumab arms.
efficacy.model: Orthotopic KRAS-WT and KRAS-mutant xenografts with NK-cell ADCC assays (GA201)
efficacy.note: GAIN-C randomized phase 2: no PFS benefit from adding imgatuzumab to FOLFIRI in KRAS-mutant (HR 0.94) and no edge over cetuximab in KRAS-WT (HR 1.13); program stopped.
efficacy.short: GAIN-C negative in KRAS-WT and mutant
efficacy.quote: The outcome was negative with respect to the primary efficacy endpoint (PFS) with no benefit seen for the addition of imgatuzumab to FOLFIRI in second-line in both KRAS e2WT and e2MT populations.

patient_trials.quote: Median PFS (Investigator reported) was 7.3 months in group 1 versus6.1 in group 2 (HR, 1.13; 95% CI 0.69-1.86) and 5.2 months in group 3 versus 4.3 in group 4 (HR, 0.94; 95% CI 0.57-1.54).

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Bleeker 2004. Registry record NCT00677924 read in full (results posted 2011-12-23).
efficacy.judgement: Untested rather than contra: the only CRC trial (phase 1/2, zalutumumab 8 or 16 mg/kg with irinotecan in cetuximab-refractory mCRC) enrolled 9 patients, had adverse events as its primary outcome, posted 0 responses and 7 stable disease, and was terminated 'due to changes in portfolio review'. No efficacy conclusion is possible and no source compares it with the A431 model; the only publication is an ASCO e-abstract (Mano 2009, e15028), not located. Zalutumumab's efficacy record (SCCHN phase 3, Machiels 2011) is another disease.
efficacy.model: A431 epidermoid xenografts in athymic mice (zalutumumab/2F8)
efficacy.note: A431 xenografts regressed on 2F8; the sole CRC trial (9 cetuximab-refractory patients, 0 responses, stopped on portfolio review) allows no comparison.
efficacy.short: A431 model; CRC trial too small to score
efficacy.quote: In vivo studies showed potent antitumor effects in models with A431 tumor xenografts in athymic mice.

patient_trials.quote: The BOR defined as the best response recorded from the start of treatment until disease progression or recurrence per RECIST criteria.

efficacy.reason: Nine-patient CRC trial, nothing to compare

efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC3950873). The paper also states 'NK cell numbers and ADCC were largely preserved in patients, regardless of their therapeutic stage, giving full scope to combining chemotherapy and ADCC-triggering immunotherapy.' GAIN-C (NCT01326000) was already recruiting (start 2011-04) when this was published.
efficacy.model: Ex-vivo NK cells from mCRC patients before, during and after chemotherapy, GA201-induced ADCC against A431 (imgatuzumab)
efficacy.note: Preserved ADCC in chemotherapy-exposed patients' NK cells was read as support for GA201 plus chemotherapy in CRC; no trial result paired yet.
efficacy.quote: These findings support the evaluation of the therapeutic potential of GA201 in combination with chemotherapy in CRC patients.
efficacy.judgement: The model's stated prediction is a combination prediction (ADCC-triggering antibody plus chemotherapy), which is exactly what GAIN-C tested; the single-agent KRAS-mutant expansion (Delord 2014, 0/25 responses) was public before the model and is not scored here.
efficacy.population: mCRC patients pre-, on- and post-chemotherapy (peripheral NK cells ex vivo)

efficacy.magnitude_basis: PFS HR 0.94 (imgatuzumab+FOLFIRI vs FOLFIRI, KRAS-mutant) and 1.13 (vs cetuximab+FOLFIRI, KRAS-WT); the ex-vivo assay gave no effect size
efficacy.confidence_note: ASCO GI 2015 meeting abstract (DOI 10.1200/jco.2015.33.3_suppl.669, online 2015-01), not a full paper; NCT01326000 (169 randomized) has no posted results and no journal publication was found. Tier 1 by its DOI, weighted as an abstract; same rule question as the draft's existing GAIN-C entry.
efficacy.model: Ex-vivo NK cells from mCRC patients before, during and after chemotherapy, GA201-induced ADCC against A431 (imgatuzumab)
efficacy.note: GAIN-C: imgatuzumab added to second-line FOLFIRI gave no PFS benefit in KRAS-mutant (HR 0.94) or over cetuximab in KRAS-WT (HR 1.13); program stopped.
efficacy.short: No benefit with chemotherapy in GAIN-C
efficacy.quote: The outcome was negative with respect to the primary efficacy endpoint (PFS) with no benefit seen for the addition of imgatuzumab to FOLFIRI in second-line in both KRAS e2WT and e2MT populations.
efficacy.judgement: The ex-vivo system predicted that preserved patient NK ADCC would let imgatuzumab add to chemotherapy; the randomized combination trial showed no PFS gain in either KRAS stratum. Paired by me: the abstract does not cite the ex-vivo paper. One drug's contra sets the track.
efficacy.reason: Chemotherapy combination gave no PFS benefit
efficacy.population: Second-line mCRC, KRAS exon 2 wild-type and mutant

efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5620195). The paper's own conclusion: Sym004 'could be a strategy to overcome acquired resistance to first generation of anti-EGFR therapies in mCRC as a result of MET activation'. The MET-activated subgroup was never tested as such in any Sym004 trial.
efficacy.model: CRC lines with acquired cetuximab resistance and MET activation (GEO-CR, SW48-CR, LIM1215-CR, CACO2-CR) and SW48 xenografts treated at progression on cetuximab (Sym004)
efficacy.note: Sym004 regressed every SW48 xenograft that had progressed on cetuximab, 4/7 still responding at 30 weeks; prediction: Sym004 overcomes acquired anti-EGFR resistance in mCRC.
efficacy.quote: Importantly, in the current work we observed a response to therapy in all cetuximab resistant tumors mice treated with SYM004.
efficacy.judgement: Different system and different prediction from the Symphogen track: acquired resistance selected against cetuximab and driven by MET, with a treat-at-progression design, where the ECD-mutant lines predicted on a different biomarker. The MET-specific (patient-level) claim stayed untested; the class-level claim was tested by the phase 2.
efficacy.population: CRC lines with in-vitro-acquired cetuximab resistance (MET-activated GEO-CR, SW48-CR; LIM1215-CR, CACO2-CR) and nude-mouse xenografts

efficacy.magnitude_basis: all cetuximab-progressed xenografts responded vs 26/39 disease control and 5/39 partial responses in patients; no shared quantity
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC5620195). The phase 1 expansion (Dienstmann 2015, Cancer Discov, online 2015-05-11; NCT01117428 results posted 2017-07-12; ASCO 2013 abstract 3551) was public before the manuscript was received (2016-12-05). Disease control, not the trial's response endpoint, is the quantity the paper compares.
efficacy.model: CRC lines with acquired cetuximab resistance and MET activation (GEO-CR, SW48-CR, LIM1215-CR, CACO2-CR) and SW48 xenografts treated at progression on cetuximab (Sym004)
efficacy.note: The paper sets its resistant-xenograft responses beside the already-published phase 1 expansion: disease control in 26/39 anti-EGFR-refractory patients, known before the model ran.
efficacy.quote: In the second Phase I trial, SYM004 achieved disease control in 26 of 39 enrolled patients with acquired resistance to anti-EGFR therapy.
efficacy.judgement: Decision 10: the acquired-resistance activity the model shows was already known in patients from the phase 1 expansion, so the model's agreement with it is a retrodiction, drawn apart from same; its prospective test is the next entry.

patient_trials.quote: In dose-expansion cohorts of 9 and 12 mg/kg of Sym004 weekly, patients with metastatic colorectal cancer and acquired EGFR inhibitor resistance were enrolled; 17 of 39 patients (44%) had tumor shrinkage, with 5 patients (13%) achieving partial response.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: OS HR 1.31 (A vs C) and 0.97 (B vs C) vs response in all cetuximab-progressed xenografts; no shared quantity
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text of Montagut 2018 read (PMC5885274; online 2018-04-12). Year 2017 follows the checker's dating (Symphogen release 2017-09; ESMO 2017 abstract 478O), not re-verified here; registry NCT02083653 results posted 2018-12-24. The model went online 2017-06-27, before the readout, so this is a prospective prediction, not a retrodiction. No Sym004 trial selected or analysed MET-activated patients.
efficacy.model: CRC lines with acquired cetuximab resistance and MET activation (GEO-CR, SW48-CR, LIM1215-CR, CACO2-CR) and SW48 xenografts treated at progression on cetuximab (Sym004)
efficacy.note: Randomized phase 2 in anti-EGFR-refractory mCRC, the model's population: OS not improved (HR 1.31 and 0.97 vs investigator's choice); MET-activated patients were never analysed.
efficacy.short: Phase 2 OS failed in acquired resistance
efficacy.quote: Sym004 did not improve OS in an unselected population of patients with mCRC and acquired anti-EGFR resistance.
efficacy.judgement: The first prospective test after the retrodiction: the model predicted Sym004 overcomes acquired anti-EGFR resistance and the randomized trial in exactly that population missed its OS primary endpoint. The exploratory ctDNA triple-negative subgroup benefit does not rescue the class call, and the MET-specific claim stays untested.

patient_trials.quote: A subgroup of patients was defined by ctDNA (RAS/BRAF/EGFR ECD-mutation negative) associated with improved OS in Sym004-treated patients in arm B compared with arm C (median OS, 12.8 and 7.3 months, respectively).

safety.judgement: Opens the safety strip with the only published toxicology for a member: 6-8 week cynomolgus repeat-dose studies of Sym004 at 2-24 mg/kg weekly with cetuximab as comparator. The monkey showed dose-related skin rash (blistering at the 36/24 mg/kg top dose), dehydration and liquid faeces; the full text does not report serum magnesium. Imgatuzumab and zalutumumab have no published toxicology to compare, so no track for them.
safety.model: Cynomolgus repeat-dose toxicology with cetuximab comparator (Sym004)
safety.note: Monkeys on 2-24 mg/kg weekly developed early, reversible, dose-related skin rash, dehydration and liquid faeces, nothing beyond the cetuximab class profile; no patient data yet.
safety.quote: However, an early onset of pronounced, reversible, and anticipated anti-EGFR-mediated pharmacologic effects, such as skin rash, dehydration, and liquid feces, was observed.

safety.magnitude_basis: skin rash in 69% of 62 patients (grade 3 skin toxicity dose-limiting) vs dose-related rash in all monkey dose groups; no incidence ratio
safety.population: KRAS exon 2 wild-type mCRC with acquired resistance to cetuximab/panitumumab
safety.confidence_note: Full text read. Hypomagnesaemia (53%, dose-limiting) was not reported in the monkey paper; cetuximab's own monkey package is also silent on it, and whether the species can show EGFR-dependent renal magnesium wasting is not established, so the silence is noted, not scored as a miss.
safety.judgement: Same: the monkey's predicted harm (dose-related skin rash) was the dose-limiting toxicity in patients, and the paper itself sets the monkey toxicology beside the clinical profile ('Toxicology studies in cynomolgus monkeys showed a toxicity profile consistent with other drugs of the same class, including dermatologic and gastrointestinal events'). Hypomagnesaemia, the second DLT, was unpredicted but is left unscored for the species reason above. Decision 16 not invoked: the harm was predicted but the monkey gave no margin.
safety.model: Cynomolgus repeat-dose toxicology with cetuximab comparator (Sym004)
safety.note: Grade 3 skin toxicity capped the phase 1 dose, as the dose-related monkey rash foretold; hypomagnesaemia (53%) was the unpredicted second dose-limiting toxicity.
safety.short: Monkey rash became the dose-limiting toxicity
safety.quote: In this phase I trial, we observed grade 3 skin toxicity and hypomagnesemia as mechanism-based dose-limiting events during dose escalation.
safety.reason: Predicted rash was dose-limiting in patients
